key_insight: The paper introduces an open-source hardware-software toolkit that automates RHEED control and analysis so AI agents can guide thin-film synthesis in real time.
engineering_relevance: It lowers the barrier to autonomous materials growth by combining programmable electron optics, automated alignment, and agent-ready interfaces for quantitative surface monitoring.
method: Programmable control of RHEED electron optics on a pulsed laser deposition system
Automated beam alignment, rocking-curve acquisition, and training-free crystallographic azimuthal alignment
Auto RHEED software with shared GUI/programmatic access plus an MCP server and extensible adapters
evidence_signal: The toolkit was demonstrated on a pulsed laser deposition system and an agent-driven workflow showed natural-language requests could select, configure, and execute quantitative analyses.
watch_item: Adoption may depend on careful integration with existing instruments and on the maturity of community-developed adapters and AI analysis methods.
paper_title: An Open-Source Hardware and Software Toolkit to Enable Agentic RHEED-Guided Thin-Film Synthesis
